summary: Wi-Fi 4-addr bridge mode on APs causes IKEv2 NAT-T negotiation failures and VPN disconnects during roaming
description: Issue summary: Several employees in the SF office reported VPN disconnects when roaming between APs on the 5GHz mesh. Symptom correlates with APs configured in bridge mode with 4-address (4addr) enabled. Impact: intermittent IKEv2 (UDP 500/4500) NAT-T negotiation failures; users experience brief drops (~10-30s) and repeated rekey attempts. No mass outage, but reproducible for specific APs and clients.
impact: Moderate internal impact: engineers lose VPN tunnel during building-level roaming and reconnects are slow. Affects productivity in-office but not remote workers. ~8 distinct reports in 48h.
environment_details: Affected SSID: redwood-corp; AP models: Aruba IAP-535 (firmware 8.5.0.3) and OpenWRT bridge nodes in meeting rooms. VPN: IKEv2 strongSwan on client and rtr-edge firewall using NAT (AWS Transit Gateway + on-prem router). Environment: prod-us-west (SF office subnet 10.24.12.0/22).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Join redwood-corp SSID on macOS Big Sur/Monterey and Ubuntu 22.04 laptops. 2) Establish IKEv2 VPN tunnel to edge. 3) Walk between two APs served by a bridge-mode WAP that has 4addr enabled (AP1 -> AP2). 4) Observe VPN rekey/teardown in client logs and intermittent 4500/500 drops in packet captures.
observed_behavior: strongSwan logs show repeated "NAT-T keepalive" and "no response to informational" then 'failed to establish CHILD_SA' messages. tcpdump on client shows UDP 4500 packets leaving with original client IP but replies arrive with bridged MAC/address mapping that conntrack considers mismatched. conntrack on router shows ephemeral NAT entries expiring when source MAC changes with 4addr bridging.
expected_behavior: IKEv2 NAT-T should survive AP-to-AP roaming with no NAT state loss; UDP packets should be correctly NATed and tolerated across layer-2 handoffs.
raw_logs_fingerprint:
strongswan-logs-snippet: 2026-03-11T15:02:12Z IKEv2[1234]: peer supports NAT-T
... INVALID_SPI / no CHILD_SA established; tcpdump-4500-snippet: OUT UDP 10.24.12.45:4500 -> 52.14.23.9:4500 (encaps)
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:20 - Triage: Collected client strongSwan logs and tcpdumps from affected user laptop.

03/10 11:40 - Observed that APs running bridge mode with 4addr send frames where the original client MAC is preserved but outer headers change; this led to the on-prem router seeing alternating source MACs during a short roam.
03/11 08:05 - Reproduced in lab by enabling 4addr on a test AP chain: immediate rekey failures observed when traffic traversed AP boundary with different bridge forwarding behavior.

03/11 10:22 - conntrack on rtr-edge shows NAT entries with src=10.24.12.45 translated->public:xxxxx; when client roamed, a second entry with same src but different layer2 arrived and conntrack timed out existing mapping causing UDP port mismatch.

03/12 14:30 - Hypothesis: 4addr causes the AP to forward frames encapsulating the L2 source in a way that interacts poorly with our NAT-T expectations; the edge NAT implementation treats the different L2 association as a new flow and clears existing translation, breaking IKEv2 keepalive continuity.
03/13 09:50 - Confirmed that disabling 4addr on AP2 eliminated the reproduction in lab; VPN stayed stable during roaming between AP1 and AP2.
03/13 15:10 - Noted that some AP firmware versions behave differently (Aruba 8.5.0.3 vs 8.4.x); Aruba's bridge proxy-arp mode maintains consistent L2 appearance.
03/14 08:00 - Eng network team suggests adding NAT tolerate option on strongSwan and increasing UDP timeout as a short-term mitigation while AP configs are remediated.
comments: Aisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Users reported VPN drops walking from north wing -> meeting rooms. Attached client logs.
Nate Huang (SRE) 2026-03-11: Got tcpdumps. Looks like 4500 keepalive replies are not matching conntrack entries after roam. Flagging network team.
Priya Rao (Wireless Eng) 2026-03-11: We have two APs in bridge mode with 4addr enabled for the mesh. Can we try disabling 4addr on the second AP as a test?
Kiran Desai (Assignee) 2026-03-12: Disabled 4addr on AP2 in meeting room A and asked affected user to reproduce. User reports stable VPN. Planning rollback to all APs in that building.

Diego Morales (Edge Eng) 2026-03-13: Added conntrack logging for UDP 4500/500; observed conntrack DELETE events corresponding to roam timestamps. Working on rule to extend NAT timeout for UDP 4500 for internal subnets.
Kiran Desai 2026-03-14: Drafted config change: disable 4addr on Aruba APs in SF, and enable 'proxy-arp' mode. Will schedule change window 2026-03-16 02:00-03:00 PT.
Priya Rao 2026-03-14: Filing follow-up firmware ticket with vendor about proxy-arp vs 4addr behavior and recommending patch. Link in related_confluence_pages.
temporary_workaround: Disable 4addr on affected APs (set APs to proxy-arp/normal bridge), or move affected APs out of mesh bridging mode. Alternatively, increase conntrack timeout for UDP 4500 on rtr-edge to 120s and enable strongSwan nat-t keepalive. Workaround applied to building A on 2026-03-13.
next_steps: 1) Execute scheduled AP config rollout to disable 4addr in SF building (2026-03-16). 2) Patch edge conntrack to extend UDP 4500 timeout and deploy strongSwan nat-t tolerate options as precaution. 3) Open vendor firmware escalation to Aruba for 4addr handling across NAT-T. 4) Add alerting for repeated conntrack DELETE on UDP 4500 for corp subnets.
resolution: In Progress - mitigation applied on a per-AP basis; full rollout and vendor follow-up pending. No code changes to core services required at this time.
